sections.html: The large halfbeaks of the genus Zenarchopterus are only very rarely offered, because the animals are very shy during acclimatisation. When they panic they often hurt themselves seriously. A small group of fully grown specimens of Zenarchopterus dunckeri was successfully imported from Taiwan. The fish are currently about 15 cm long. The group is formed of two males and three females.

These fish need very clean, bacteria-poor, hard water. The pH must be over 8. They are completely euryhaline and can also be kept in brackish or pure seawater, but an addition of salt is not absolutely essential.
The fish prefer flake foods, but also accept other food items as long as they are floating on the water surface. Once the food has sunk to the bottom it is ignored.

Choose only absolutely peaceful tankmates for cleaning the tank of sunken food, for example Corys, because even harmless but curious fish can literally frighten the halfbeaks witless. Once Zenarchopterus have settled, they can live happily for many years in aquaria.
